result.topic_en: A numerical calculation of one Newton-type correction step for a complex root of a polynomial with terms 4x^5, 5x^4, 40x^3, 10x^2 and constant −500, starting from x = 0.9 + 2.8i; the arithmetic uses logarithms and angles in degrees, minutes and seconds.

methods.what: Evaluation of the polynomial terms and their sum at a complex point, using logarithms of the modulus and angles in degrees, minutes and seconds
Computation of x f'(x) at x = 0.9 + 2.8i by summing the complex components of each term
Obtaining f'(x) from x f'(x) by dividing by x in polar/logarithmic form (subtracting the angle and the log modulus)
A direct computation of f'(x) as a check
Value of the derivative at the trial point
Newton correction −f(x)/f'(x), computed in polar form and then converted to rectangular form
New approximation of the root: x − f(x)/f'(x)
